ethics: Ninety-eight agents have come through this branch in the sixteen years the record covers. Sixty resigned. There were four retirements, three left vested, and three transferred inside Guardian. And in all that time, four terminations.

You hear about the quotas. You never hear what this branch stands for. Your client reads the plan and approves it before a manager signs it. Every paper logged. Every call logged. And nobody is above it, from the top producer to the newest agent.

The Central Bank's market conduct code is not something we check afterwards. It is built into every letter, every form and every advertisement we put out. We do not quote a section we cannot stand behind. We do not print a figure we invented. And no policy is changed before the advantages and the disadvantages are put to the client.

So ask the question the other way round. If the Central Bank walked in here tomorrow, what could we hand them? Fact finds the client signed and a manager signed off. Two thousand one hundred and ninety-one cash approvals on record. Minutes inside thirty minutes. Fifty processes, every one of them auditable. Most branches cannot produce that.

Now, do things go wrong here? Things go wrong in every branch. Two thousand one hundred and ninety-one cash approvals is how a problem becomes visible in the first place. And when we found one, here is exactly what we did. We found it. We investigated it. We called the client ourselves. We recovered the money. And we put the whole record on file.

And here is the part people miss. Seventy-six have left over those sixteen years. A standard costs you people. Nobody here is kept by being allowed to do as they please. We have paid that price, and we would pay it again.

We have been through this before. In two thousand and twenty a group of our agents left together for a competitor. That was thirteen people in one year, and this branch went from forty down to twenty-seven. Four years later we were back to thirty-nine.

It is not unusual and it is not only us. The research outside says most of a book stays with the firm when the adviser goes. About forty per cent of client assets follow the person. What decides the rest is whether anybody calls the client.

So this is how we rebuild. Hold the book by serving it, not by asking anyone to stay. Every household written to and matched to an agent. Every premium chased. And we select the people who come next. We do not fill seats.
